items.title: I don't enjoy being pampered
items.brief_zh: 作者在维尔纽斯理发时被做了一整套热敷、按摩和修面服务，他觉得自己只是忍受，并不享受，于是想弄清楚原因。
items.brief_en: The author got a long barber session with hot towels, massage and shaving in Vilnius. He felt he only tolerated it, and he wonders why.
detail_zh: 作者在维尔纽斯度假时觉得胡子太长，天气快热起来了，他就走进遇到的第一家理发店，请师傅把胡子剪回夏天的长度。理发师让他躺平，先用热毛巾和冷毛巾敷脸，蒸胡子并梳理，又按摩头部和肩膀，涂上各种膏和香味的发蜡，最后用几把剃刀修整。整个过程接近一个小时。
作者说，他其实并不享受这种服务。闻起来香、看起来整齐当然是好事，他也不反感在便宜的店里五分钟刮完胡子。但长达一个小时的被伺候，让他只能说是忍受。染头发时他也是同样的感觉。他问自己，是不是不喜欢陌生人碰自己，或者觉得自己不配得到这样的放松和享受。
相比之下，两年前他去做牙科手术，反而觉得有种奇怪的舒服。他平躺着闭上眼睛，一小组专业人员在他身上忙活，那一刻他既觉得完全无力，又觉得非常安全。他由此理解了为什么有人会假装生病，把自己交给外科医生。他觉得物理治疗让人放松，但讨厌被按摩，一想到修脚就很反感。
他想，也许是因为他把头发看成了虚荣的装饰，而沉迷虚荣是不光彩的，屈服于肉体的毛病却只是凡人而已。他对验光师和肛肠科医生做的检查没有意见。他问，物理治疗师捏他的脚是为了治病，修脚师修指甲、磨老茧，两者之间到底有什么区别？最后他说，自己的脑子大概有点怪，并且打算买一个适合旅行带的修剪器。
detail_en: On holiday in Vilnius, the author found his beard too long for a coming heatwave. He went into the first barber he saw and asked for it to be cut back to summer length. The barber reclined the chair, used hot and cold towels, steamed and brushed the beard, massaged his head and shoulders, applied scented pomades, and shaved with several razors. The whole thing took close to an hour.

The author says he did not really enjoy it. Smelling nice and looking neat were good, and he does not mind a quick five-minute shave at a cheap shop. But an hour of being pampered left him only tolerating it. He felt much the same when he got his hair dyed. He wonders whether he just dislikes strangers touching him, or whether he feels he does not deserve this kind of indulgence.

By contrast, he found dental surgery two years ago strangely pleasant. Lying flat with his eyes closed while a small team worked on him made him feel both vulnerable and very safe. This helped him understand why some people fake illness to be cared for by surgeons. He finds physiotherapy relaxing and massage unpleasant, and the idea of a pedicure fills him with horror.

He wonders if he sees his hair as a vanity. Giving in to vanity seems unworthy, while giving in to the failings of the flesh is merely mortal. He has no problem with opticians or proctologists. He asks whether a physio treating his foot is really different from a pedicurist filing his nails and calluses. He concludes that his brain is weird and that he needs a travel-sized beard trimmer.

items.title: Mouse for Tandy 1000
items.brief_zh: 作者介绍了几种适合早期 Tandy 1000 使用的鼠标，原装 TRS-80 彩色鼠标很难找也很贵，所以他更推荐串口鼠标和 Tandy 或 Radio Shack 的品牌鼠标。
items.brief_en: The author lists mouse options for the early Tandy 1000. The original TRS-80 color mouse is hard to find and expensive, so he suggests serial mice and Tandy or Radio Shack branded mice instead.
detail_zh: 严格来说，早期 Tandy 1000 正统的鼠标是 TRS-80 彩色鼠标，型号是 26-3025。它是黑色的，只有一个红色按键，外形方方正正。它其实用两个电位器工作，更像模拟摇杆，而不是普通鼠标，所以需要 Tandy 自己的驱动程序。它插在摇杆接口上，因此即使是没有扩展的早期 Tandy 1000 也能用。
不过这种鼠标很难找，价格也高，所以作者换了一条路。如果机器装有 RS-232 串口，任何 9 针的串口鼠标都能用。例如微软的 Dove bar 鼠标，年代相符、好找又便宜；早期的罗技鼠标也很合适。

如果想要配色统一，Radio Shack 卖过 Tandy 品牌的鼠标。最正宗的是 25-1040D，但更难找。后来 Tandy 品牌的罗技鼠标 25-2001 外观和 Compaq、Dell 随机附送的一样，只是印了 Tandy 的标志，大约 25 美元。Tandy 退出电脑业务后，Radio Shack 改卖 IBM 和 Compaq 的电脑，但仍然卖配件，多半印 Radio Shack 的标志。例如 RS-232 鼠标 26-326，现在大约 15 美元，疫情期间曾经卖到 40 多美元。它年代晚一些，但放在 Tandy 1000 旁边看起来还是对得上。
后来的串口鼠标几乎能配任何鼠标驱动，这是它的优势。Tandy 1000 内存比较紧张，而 ctmouse 只需要 6K，用它就方便很多。Radio Shack 后来的鼠标其实还是换了标志的罗技产品，只是外观按当时的样式稍微更新了。这篇文章是作者关于 Tandy 和 Radio Shack 系列中的一篇。
detail_en: The proper mouse for early Tandy 1000 models is the TRS-80 color mouse, part number 26-3025. It is black with one red button and a squared-off shape. It uses two potentiometers, so it works more like an analog joystick than a normal mouse, and it needs Tandy's driver. It plugs into the joystick port, so it works even on unexpanded early Tandy 1000s.

The author did not choose this mouse because it is hard to find and expensive. Instead he took another route. If the machine has an RS-232 serial port, any 9-pin serial mouse will work. Examples include the Microsoft Dove bar mouse, which is period-correct, easy to find and cheap, and early Logitech mice.

If you want matching hardware, Radio Shack sold Tandy-branded mice. The most period-correct one is catalog number 25-1040D, but it is harder to find. Later Tandy-branded Logitech mice, such as 25-2001, look just like the Logitech mice sold by Compaq and Dell, with a Tandy logo. They cost about 25 dollars. After Tandy left the computer business, Radio Shack sold IBM and Compaq computers and kept selling accessories, usually with Radio Shack branding. An RS-232 mouse such as 26-326 costs about 15 dollars now, though it rose above 40 dollars during the pandemic. It is from a later decade but still looks right next to a Tandy 1000.

A later serial mouse works with almost any mouse driver you want. This matters because Tandy 1000s have limited memory, and ctmouse needs only 6K. The later Radio Shack mice are relabeled Logitech units with styling updated for their production period. The post is part of the author's series on Tandy and Radio Shack.

items.title: Weekly Update 531: Optimizely. Script Dependencies & Third Parties
items.brief_zh: Troy Hunt 在本期周更中指出，把数据交给第三方并不能推卸公司的责任，并以 Optimizely 的一起事件为例说明。
items.brief_en: Troy Hunt argues that giving data to a third party does not remove the accountability of the company that holds it. He uses the Optimizely incident as an example.
detail_zh: “你不能把责任外包”。但当泄露通知说事件“发生在第三方”时，听起来就像是在推卸责任，好像这样说就好受一些。作者认为，责任最终仍在把数据交给对方的那一方身上，而决定是否公开事件的，也是他们。就这次 Optimizely 的事件来说，作者说这显然是 Optimizely 的问题，但挪威航空之类的客户要自己决定是否联系受影响的人。而挪威航空还没有点名那家第三方。
detail_en: "You can't outsource accountability." The author says that when a disclosure notice says an incident was at a third party, it seems to deflect responsibility, as if that makes it better. Accountability still rests with the party that was trusted with the data, and that party is also the one who decides whether to disclose the incident. He says the Optimizely incident is clearly Optimizely's fault, yet customers such as Norwegian Airlines must decide whether to contact the people affected. Norwegian Airlines has not named the third party.

items.title: To code well, avoid blunders
items.brief_zh: 作者认为写好代码的关键是避免灾难性失误，尤其是前后不一致和加入不必要的需求，而不是想出聪明的技巧。
items.brief_en: The author argues that good code comes from avoiding big mistakes, especially inconsistency and unnecessary requirements, not from clever ideas.
detail_zh: 作者说，写好代码的秘诀是避免灾难性的失误。很多工程师以为要靠精彩的洞见，但作者认为只要不犯大错，就能赢。下棋时如果从不丢子，就能赢过几乎所有对手；网球里如果回球很稳，即使打不出致胜球，也能赢过大多数人。大家常以为要靠漂亮的战术或者重炮式的进攻，这些都有价值，但都不是最重要的。

作者解释说，编程之所以如此，是因为很难建立持久的领先优势。篮球比赛里，即使领先 99 比 1，最糟的失误也只是变成 99 比 4。但在编程里，一个失误就能把优雅的代码库变成一团乱麻。他认为最严重的是两类错误：前后不一致，以及引入不必要的需求。不一致会破坏信任，让工程师必须到处找意外。不必要的需求则有两个问题：一是很难清除，因为除非花很多时间去研究，否则看到代码里的需求只能默认它是必要的；二是它们会互相影响，每新增一个功能，都要考虑它和已有功能之间的关系，组合起来非常复杂，这就是大型代码库难以驾驭的原因。
因此，作者认为写代码时要尽全力避免这些错误，也就没有精力去想巧妙的技巧或额外的功能。如果发现自己在想“这里可以用一个巧妙的模式来实现”，就是一个警示，说明注意力已经被转移，可能要犯错了。他认为好的编程工作不需要聪明，有时聪明反而是负担。真正需要的是注意细节，专注于最重要的事：保持一致，不加不必要的需求。
作者说，他主要谈的是大团队在大型商业代码库上的工作，也就是他所说的“不纯粹的工程”，换成其他类型的工作，这些建议未必适用。他还说，不论是手写代码还是驱动 AI 代理，道理都一样。他猜测，从不犯错大概能让人达到 1600 到 1700 的国际象棋等级分，足以赢过大多数休闲棋手。关于 AI 编码代理，他认为它们在保持一致方面和人差不多，但在避免不必要的需求方面要差得多。
detail_en: The author says the secret to good code is to avoid catastrophic mistakes. Many engineers think brilliant insight matters most, but he believes that not blundering is what wins. A chess player who never hangs pieces will beat almost any opponent. A tennis player who returns balls reliably will beat most people even without winners. Brilliant tactics and powerful shots are valuable, but they are not the main thing.

Programming is like this because it is hard to build a lasting lead. In basketball, if you lead 99 to 1, the worst blunder still leaves you at 99 to 4. In code, one blunder can turn an elegant codebase into a messy one. The two worst mistakes are inconsistency and unnecessary requirements. Inconsistency breaks trust, so engineers must hunt for surprises. Unnecessary requirements are hard to remove, because unless you spend a lot of time researching, you must assume they are needed. They also interact: each new feature must be checked against existing ones, and the combinations grow quickly. This is why large codebases are hard to work in.

So when writing code, he says you should try hard to avoid these mistakes. You then have little energy left for clever tricks or extra features. If you catch yourself thinking you could use a clever pattern, that is a warning sign that you are getting distracted and may make a mistake. He says you do not need to be clever to do good work, and cleverness can even be a disadvantage. What you need is attention to detail and a clear focus on keeping things consistent and skipping unnecessary requirements.

He says he is mainly talking about large commercial codebases with big teams, which he calls impure engineering, and the advice may not apply to other kinds of work. He adds that the same points apply whether you write code by hand or drive an AI agent. He guesses that never blundering would earn a chess rating of about 1600 to 1700, which is strong enough to beat most casual players. He also notes that current coding agents are about as good as humans at consistency but much worse at avoiding unnecessary requirements.

items.title: Muru
items.brief_zh: Graham Dumpleton 正在用 AI 辅助开发一个名为 Muru 的 Rust 服务器，用来运行 ASGI 和 WSGI 的 Python 应用。Simon Willison 推荐其中一篇谈 AI 与个人投入的文章。
items.brief_en: Graham Dumpleton is building Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for running Python ASGI and WSGI apps. Simon Willison recommends one of his posts about AI and personal effort.
detail_zh: Muru 是 Graham Dumpleton 的新项目，是一个借助 AI 开发的 Rust 服务器，目标是在开发和生产环境中为 ASGI 与 WSGI 形式的 Python 应用提供尽可能好的运行工具。和他之前的 wrapture 项目一样，作者在开发过程中公开了非常详细的记录，这也是他开发流程的一部分。Simon Willison 这篇短文列出了作者最近三周内发布的所有相关文章。
Simon 特别推荐其中一篇讨论把 AI 当作一种生活方式选择的文章。作者在文中说，表面上的很多工作可以交给 AI 完成，但判断什么还不够好，仍然要由他自己决定。他做了二十年 mod_wsgi，犯过不少错，这些经验在做判断时很有用。他表示愿意投入大量辛苦的工作，把 Muru 打磨到他自己和读者都能信任的程度。
detail_en: Muru is a new project from Graham Dumpleton. It is a Rust server built with AI assistance, aimed at giving the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps in both development and production. As with his earlier wrapture project, the author is publishing a detailed account of the work as he goes, as part of his development process. Simon Willison's short post lists everything the author published in the last three weeks.

Simon especially recommends a post about treating AI as a lifestyle choice. The author says AI may do much of the visible work, but deciding what is not yet good enough is still his job. Twenty years of mistakes with mod_wsgi are useful for that judgment. He says he is willing to put in hard work to polish Muru until he and the reader would both trust it.

items.title: Notes on the discrete Fourier transform (DFT)
items.brief_zh: 这篇笔记介绍有限长离散信号的离散傅里叶变换（DFT），说明它与 DTFT 的关系、矩阵形式、逆变换，以及频谱泄漏问题。
items.brief_en: This note explains the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) for finite signals. It covers how the DFT relates to the DTFT, the matrix view, the inverse, and spectral leakage.
detail_zh: 上一篇讨论了离散时间傅里叶级数（DTFS）和离散时间傅里叶变换（DTFT），它们处理的是无限长的信号。这篇转向实际的数字信号处理，信号既是离散的，又是有限长的。作者手里只有一串采样值，想找出其中包含的频率成分。如果假设采样之外的值都是零，直接用 DTFT，结果是一个关于频率的连续函数，无法在计算机上完整保存，必须选若干频率点来计算。
另一种思路是把这 N 个采样看成某个周期信号的一个周期。这样就可以使用 DTFS，它能精确重建离散周期信号。这就是离散傅里叶变换（DFT）的核心想法。作者指出，DFT 其实就是 DTFT 在等间隔频率点上的采样。
作者给出了两种计算方式。一种是按公式逐个频率求和的 Python 函数，另一种是用傅里叶矩阵乘以信号向量。矩阵的每一行由单位根的幂组成，前文已经证明这些行构成正交基，所以任何复数向量都能写成它们的线性组合。DFT 就是把信号投影到这组基上。NumPy 的向量化让第二种写法很简洁。
关于逆变换，作者给出两种推导。一种直接从 DTFS 的重建公式得到。另一种利用线性代数：傅里叶矩阵的共轭矩阵与它相乘，结果是单位矩阵的常数倍，因此傅里叶矩阵可逆，逆变换与 DTFS 得到的公式相同。作者认为用两种方法得到同一结果是个好兆头。

例子部分用一个 12 点的三角波周期，两种计算方法结果一致，逆变换能把原信号精确恢复，误差只来自浮点舍入。NumPy 的 fft 函数实现了快速傅里叶变换（FFT），利用傅里叶矩阵的结构把计算量从 N² 降到 N log N，作者说以后会单独讲。附录讨论频谱泄漏：如果只取三角波的前 10 个采样，周期延拓时边界会出现跳变，原本的频率不再落在 DFT 的频点上，能量会散布到多个频点。逆变换仍然能精确恢复这 10 个采样，但做频率分析时会引入并不存在的频率。实际中常用窗函数对信号做渐变处理，以减轻泄漏。
detail_en: The previous post covered the DTFS and DTFT, which apply to infinite-length signals. This post turns to real digital signal processing, where signals are both discrete and finite. The author has only a list of samples and wants the frequencies in them. If you assume the signal is zero outside the samples and use the DTFT, the result is a continuous function of frequency. A computer cannot store that for every frequency, so you must pick specific frequencies to evaluate.

A different approach treats the N samples as one period of a periodic signal. Then the DTFS can reconstruct the signal exactly. This is the core idea of the discrete Fourier transform (DFT). The author notes that the DFT is simply the DTFT sampled at equally spaced frequencies.

The author gives two ways to compute it. One is a Python function that sums directly for each frequency. The other multiplies the signal vector by the Fourier matrix. Each row of that matrix holds powers of a root of unity. The earlier post showed these rows form an orthogonal basis, so any complex vector is a linear combination of them. The DFT is the projection onto that basis. NumPy's vectorization makes the matrix version short.

For the inverse, the author gives two derivations. One comes directly from the DTFS reconstruction formula. The other uses linear algebra. Multiplying the Fourier matrix by its conjugate gives a constant multiple of the identity matrix, so the Fourier matrix is invertible. The inverse formula matches the one from the DTFS. The author says getting the same result by two methods is a good sign.

The worked example uses one cycle of a sampled triangle wave with 12 points. Both methods give the same DFT, and the inverse recovers the original signal, with differences only from floating point rounding. NumPy's fft function implements the Fast Fourier Transform, which uses the structure of the Fourier matrix to reduce the cost from N² to N log N. The author plans a future post on it. The appendix covers spectral leakage. If you take only the first 10 samples of the triangle wave, periodic extension creates a jump at the boundary. The original frequencies no longer fall on DFT bins, so energy spreads across many bins. The inverse still recovers the 10 samples exactly, but frequency analysis shows frequencies that were not in the original wave. Window functions that taper the signal near its edges are a common way to reduce leakage.

items.title: ★ A Week With the New Privacy Controls in MacOS 27.3 Beta 2
items.brief_zh: Gruber 用一周时间试用 macOS 27.3 测试版的新隐私控制，认为整体改进是成功的，但对常驻应用触发的菜单栏指示器很不满意。
items.brief_en: Gruber spent a week with the new macOS 27.3 beta privacy controls. He thinks the overall changes are a win, but he dislikes the always-on indicator that appears when one app controls another.
detail_zh: Gruber 在 macOS 27.3 第二个测试版发布时写过 Apple 新增隐私控制的文章。背景是 Meta 的 Muse 应用获得“完全磁盘访问”权限后，被发现能读取一些用户的信息，例如收到的 iMessage，而不少用户在授权时直接点了通过。Apple 此前承诺过这项改进，并发布了相关支持文档。作者试用一周后认为，这次对设置和权限的调整是个成功。他特别喜欢的一点是，对于请求完全磁盘访问的应用，用户现在可以只授权一组指定的文件夹，这让用户拥有更多控制权。

关于新对话框是否“太吓人”，作者的看法是：它们确实更醒目，也应该如此，应用请求权限时用户应该被提醒一下。描述准确，而且不过分。对话框会展示个人照片的缩略图，虽然有冲击，但这是把抽象的“完全磁盘访问”变得具体。作者认为这可能会让一些用户不愿意把这项权限交给 AI 代理应用，但真正了解风险的用户仍会按自己的需要授权。他还认为新对话框的设计很好，更接近 macOS 的系统界面风格，而不是 iPhone 式的小提醒框。

作者唯一的不满是新的菜单栏指示器。当一个应用控制另一个应用时，它会出现，而且无法关闭，只能通过一个未公开的隐藏 defaults 设置来关闭。在带 Dynamic Island 的新款 MacBook Pro 上，指示器会显示在 Dynamic Island 里。作者引用 Chance Miller 的看法，认为这个功能太激进。Miller 的电脑上同时有 8 个这样的指示器，都来自常驻运行的工具，例如 Scroll Reverser、Keyboard Maestro Engine、HazeOver 等。作者认为，如果这些指示器一直亮着，用户反而可能忽略真正异常的访问行为。9to5Mac 的 Zac Hall 周二发文介绍了用命令行 defaults 关闭它的方法。作者觉得这比完全不能关闭要好，但预计 Apple 会根据反馈修改。他认为这个功能出发点是好的，只是设计者没有意识到很多常驻工具都会“控制其他应用”。
detail_en: Gruber wrote about Apple's new privacy controls when the second macOS 27.3 beta came out. The background is that Meta's Muse app, after getting Full Disk Access, was found to reach information such as incoming iMessages, and some users had clicked through the permission without thinking. Apple had promised these changes and published support documents. After a week of use, the author says the overhaul is a win. He especially likes that apps requesting Full Disk Access can now be granted access to a chosen list of folders instead, which gives users more control.

On whether the new dialogs are too scary, the author says they should be scarier. The descriptions are fair and accurate. The dialogs show thumbnails of personal photos. That is a jolt, but it makes the abstract phrase Full Disk Access concrete. He says this may discourage some users from granting the permission to AI agent apps, and he thinks that is appropriate. Users who understand the risks will still grant it when they want to. He also finds the new dialogs well designed, closer to modern macOS system styling than to small iPhone-style alerts.

His one complaint is the new menu bar indicator that appears when one app controls another. It cannot be turned off, except through an undocumented hidden defaults setting. On new MacBook Pros with Dynamic Island, the indicator appears there. He quotes Chance Miller, who calls it too aggressive. Miller has eight of these indicators on his Mac, all from utilities that run all the time, including Scroll Reverser, Keyboard Maestro Engine, and HazeOver. The author argues that when these indicators are always on, users may miss the real unusual activity. Zac Hall at 9to5Mac published a command-line defaults command to disable it on Tuesday. The author says that is better than nothing but expects Apple to revisit the feature. He thinks it was well intended, but its designers did not foresee how many always-on utilities control other apps.

items.title: The U.S. — Utterly Predictably — Has Lost Measles Elimination Status Under Trump and RFK Jr.
items.brief_zh: Gruber 转引《华尔街日报》的报道，说美国已失去麻疹消除状态，专家估计重新获得可能需要约五年，取决于联邦政府是否积极推动接种。
items.brief_en: Gruber quotes a Wall Street Journal report that the US has lost its measles elimination status. Doctors estimate regaining it could take about five years, depending on federal action.
detail_zh: Gruber 转引 Sumathi Reddy 为《华尔街日报》写的文章。文章说，美国失去“麻疹消除”状态是一次重大的公共卫生挫败，接下来的问题是需要多久才能重新获得。医生和流行病学家根据其他国家的经验估计，可能要五年，但这一估计假设联邦政府是积极主动推动麻疹疫苗接种的参与者。如果政府不这样做，时间可能还会更长。
文章标题用了 Utterly Predictably（完全可以预料）来形容这一结果，并写明它发生在 Trump 和 RFK Jr. 的任期内。Gruber 还引用了 Nilay Patel 两年前支持 Kamala Harris 时的文章标题：“A Vote for Donald Trump Is a Vote for School Shootings and Measles”。
detail_en: Gruber quotes Sumathi Reddy's Wall Street Journal article. It says losing measles elimination status is a major public health defeat, and the question is how long it will take to regain. Doctors and epidemiologists, based on other countries' experience, estimate up to five years. That estimate assumes the federal government actively takes part in measles vaccination. Without that, it could take longer.

The post's title uses the phrase Utterly Predictably to describe the outcome, and says it happened under Trump and RFK Jr. Gruber also quotes Nilay Patel's headline from two years ago, endorsing Kamala Harris: “A Vote for Donald Trump Is a Vote for School Shootings and Measles.”

items.title: Apple Documents Extra Apple Intelligence Usage Limits Per iCloud+ Paid Tier
items.brief_zh: 苹果支持文档说明，从2027年的系统版本起，Siri AI和Apple Intelligence功能免费提供，但部分依赖云端大模型的功能设有每日用量上限，订阅合格的iCloud+套餐可以提高上限。
items.brief_en: Apple's support page says that from the 2027 releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence are free, but some server-based features have daily usage limits that eligible iCloud+ plans can raise.
detail_zh: 苹果支持文档写道，从2027年的系统更新开始，Siri AI和Apple Intelligence功能对符合条件的设备和支持的语言免费开放。有些功能需要调用服务器上的大模型，所以设有使用限制。从27.3版本开始，订阅符合条件的iCloud+套餐的用户可以获得更高的额度。文中列出的功能类别包括：Siri AI；图像类功能，如智能照片编辑工具（清理、扩展、空间重构）和Image Playground；快捷指令里的AFM Cloud和Cloud Pro模型；第三方应用通过Private Cloud Compute调用Apple Foundation Models。文档说明这些只是部分例子，并不是全部。
每台设备、每个功能类别各自有每日用量上限。用户达到某个类别的上限时会收到通知。之后可以等当天额度重置，也可以直接升级到符合条件的iCloud+套餐，立即提高上限。
原文提到“以下是苹果按套餐列出的用量上限表”，但摘录中没有这张表，所以各档套餐的具体数字无法从这段文字看出。摘录中间还有省略（[...]）。
detail_en: Apple's support page says that starting with the 2027 software releases, Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are free for users with a supported device set to a supported language. Some features rely on powerful server models, so they have limits. From the 27.3 release, subscribers to eligible iCloud+ plans can get higher limits. The listed feature categories are Siri AI; image features such as Intelligent Photo Editing Tools (Clean Up, Extend, Spatial Reframing) and Image Playground; the AFM Cloud and Cloud Pro models in Shortcuts; and third-party apps that use Apple Foundation Models through Private Cloud Compute. The page says this list is not complete.

Each device has its own daily limit for each feature category. When a user hits the limit for a category, they get a notification. They can then wait for the daily limit to reset, or upgrade to an eligible iCloud+ plan to raise the limit right away.

The text says "here's Apple's table with the usage limits by tier," but the table is not in the excerpt, so the specific limits for each tier cannot be seen here. The excerpt also has an omission in the middle, marked [...].
